hook: The police said the offence is **non-bailable.**
hook_q: What's the difference between bailable and non-bailable?

slides.title: The law's **Schedule** decides.
slides.body: A bailable offence is one shown as bailable in the BNSS First Schedule, or made bailable by another law. Every other offence is non-bailable.

slides.title: Bailable? Bail is **your right.**
slides.body: In bailable offences, bail is the right of the accused. The police can also grant bail at the time of arrest or detention.
slides.ref: BNSS 2023 · Sec 478 · Uttarakhand Judicial & Legal Academy

slides.title: Police must **tell you.**
slides.body: If police arrest you without a warrant and you're not accused of a non-bailable offence, they must tell you that you're entitled to bail and can arrange sureties.

slides.title: Non-bailable? Bail is **not automatic.**
slides.body: Bail isn't a matter of right. It is at the discretion of the court or police officer, depending on the facts of the case. It is not ruled out.
slides.ref: BNSS 2023 · Sec 480 · Uttarakhand Judicial & Legal Academy

slides.title: Some examples from **the Schedule:**
list: Bailable: rash driving on a public way (BNS 281)

slides.title: Check **the First Schedule.**
slides.body: For each BNS offence, the First Schedule has a column saying "Bailable" or "Non-bailable". It's the quickest way to know which one applies.

sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 2(1)(c), 47(2) (indiacode.nic.in; NCRB, ncrb.mha.gov.in)
Uttarakhand Judicial & Legal Academy – Handbook on Procedure Related to Criminal Courts (on Sec 478, 480)
caption:
Bailable or non-bailable? Here's the difference. 👇

1️⃣ Bailable means the BNSS First Schedule (or another law) says so. All other offences are non-bailable
2️⃣ In bailable offences, bail is the right of the accused, and police can grant it too
3️⃣ Arrested without a warrant for a bailable offence? Police must tell you that you're entitled to bail
4️⃣ Non-bailable doesn't mean no bail. It's at the discretion of the court or police officer
5️⃣ Examples: hurt and rash driving are bailable. Murder and rape are non-bailable

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 2(1)(c), 47(2), 478, 480, First Schedule
